newsitem.title: USA: U.S. EPA to forward air rule proposal in two weeks.
newsitem.headline: U.S. EPA to forward air rule proposal in two weeks.

text.p: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency plans to send its final recommendation on new air quality standards to the White House Office of Management and Budget in about two weeks, EPA Administrator Carol Browner said Wednesday.

Browner earlier had said the final recommendation was supposed to get to the OMB around May 20 to be reviewed by other departments and agencies. But she said instead the administration is conducting its inter-agency review as the EPA prepares its recommendation.

At a panel discussion on the air standards proposal, Browner said she still has not made a decision on new standards for smog and soot pollution. But in the discussion with representatives of industry groups that oppose the EPA's proposed stricter standards, she defended the need for stronger rules.

The administration is to announce a final rule in July. Because of the intense interest in the issue, it is taking the unusual step of having the White House's National Economic Council participate in the review.

"Because of the interest of a large number of other federal agencies and departments, the NEC has stepped in to help facilitate the dialogue. We welcome that. We think it's an important part of the process," Browner said.
